LuaFunction.Name: NOBN_trk_getFarthestFoulingPoint()
LuaFunction.ReturnType: Fouling point data structure or an error message String
LuaFunction.Description:
Returns the getFoulingPoints() data structure (see F1) for the fouling point (FP) located *farthest* from the stock rail joint. 
 
FoulingPoint : Triplet {X,Y,Z) in world coordinates. 
ClearanceDistance : FP's 2D straight-line distance from stock rail joint. This is also the FP's NorRailView 'Position'. 
FoulingDistance : The sum of the lateral offsets from FP to its Branch1 and to its Branch2. 
 
Branch1 : FP's linear address relative to the switch object's Branch1 alignment. 
Branch1.AlignmentRef : - Branch1 alignment's object reference. 
Branch1.Mileage : - Mileage in Branch1. 
Branch1.Point : - Triplet (X, Y, Z), the FP's projection onto Branch1. 
Branch1.ReferenceMileage : - Reference mileage calculated via Branch1. 
 
Branch2 : FP's linear address relative to the switch object's Branch2 alignment. 
Branch2.AlignmentRef : - Branch2 alignment's object reference. 
Branch2.Mileage : - Mileage in Branch2. 
Branch2.Point : - Triplet (X, Y, Z), the FP's projection onto Branch2. 
Branch2.ReferenceMileage : - Reference mileage calculated via Branch2. 
 
Usage: NOBN_trk_getFoulingPoint(integer fpMethod, tSwitch swRef = this) 
 
where swRef is an optional reference to a switch object and fpMethod is mandatory, being one of 1, 2, 3 or 4, meaning: 
 1 New line, train/*, 
 2 New line, shunt/shunt, 
 3 Existing line, train/* 
 4 Existing line, shunt/shunt,
LuaFunction.Formula: function NOBN_trk_getFarthestFoulingPoint(fpMethod, sw) --Note: fpMethods must be spelled exactly as shown in RC-Settings - see those declarations in NO-BN.Foulingpoint.xml. --TODO: Replace (when ready) with code exploiting a new feature in getFoulingPoints() code that accesses FP methods directly. local fpMethods = { "1 New line, train/*", "2 New line, shunt/shunt", "3 Existing line, train/*", "4 Existing line, shunt/shunt" } sw = sw or this fpMethod = math.floor(fpMethod) or 1 if fpMethod < 1 or fpMethod > 4 then return "Bad fouling point method index ["..fpMethod.."] - 1, 2, 3 or 4 was expected." end if sw.RcType ~= rctype_Switch then return "Bad object type ["..sw.RcType.."], '"..rctype_Switch.."' was expected." else local fp, nFp fp, nFp = getFoulingPoints(fpMethods[fpMethod], sw) --These are already sorted on ClearanceDistance byAscending. if nFp == 0 then return "(no fouling points found)" else return fp[nFp-1] end end end

LuaFunction.Name: _JBTKO_SPF_code()
LuaFunction.Description: Returns a formated string containing the code properties '[Code1] --- [Code2]' for the two tracks that meet in a track continuation.
LuaFunction.Formula: function _JBTKO_SPF_code() local first, second if RcType ~= rctype_TrackContinuation then return _error, "Bad object type ["..RcType.."] - '"..rctype_TrackContinuation.."' was expected." else first = Alignment if first == nil then return "Bad or missing alignment reference",_warning elseif Alignment.RcType ~= rctype_Track then return "Cannot connect to alignments of type '"..Alignment.RcType.."'.",_warning end second = TargetAlignment if second == nil then return "Bad or missing continuing alignment reference",_warning elseif TargetAlignment.RcType ~= rctype_Track then return "Cannot connect to alignments of type '"..TargetAlignment.RcType.."'.",_warning end if first.id == second.id then return _error, "Own alignment and continuing alignment cannot be the same ["..first.code.."]" end --2021-08-23 CLFEY: Leave the text as-is, emphasize showing what is own / what is target: --if MileageIncreasesTowardsLeft then -- first, second = second, first --end return "["..first.code.."] ==> ["..second.code.."]" end end

LuaFunction.Name: _JBTKO_SPV_crossingCode()
LuaFunction.Description: Returns a formated string containing the code properties '[Code1] -X- [Code2]' for the two tracks that meet in a track crossing.
LuaFunction.Formula: function _JBTKO_SPV_crossingCode() local first, second if RcType ~= rctype_SwitchCrossing then return "Bad object type ["..RcType.."], '"..rctype_SwitchCrossing.."' was expected." else first = Alignment if first == nil then return "Bad or missing alignment reference",_warning end second = TargetAlignment if second == nil then return "Bad or missing intersecting alignment reference",_warning end if first.id == second.id then return "Alignment and intersecting alignment cannot be the same ["..first.code.."]" end if MileageIncreasesTowardsLeft then first, second = second, first end return "["..first.code.."] -X- ["..second.code.."]" end end

M='Machine locked (using a point machine or clamping device, with end position detection)'. L='Keylocked for left switch leg train movements'. R='Keylocked for right switch leg train movements'. LuaFunction.Formula: function _JBTKO_SPV_switchCode() local first, second if RcType ~= rctype_Switch then return "Bad object type ["..RcType.."], '"..rctype_Switch.."' was expected" else first = Alignment if first == nil then return "Bad or missing alignment reference",_warning end second = TargetAlignment if second == nil then return "Bad or missing branching alignment reference",_warning end if first.id == second.id then return "Alignment and branching alignment cannot be the same ["..first.code.."]" end return "["..Alignment.code.."] -> ["..TargetAlignment.code.."]" end end

function _JBTKO_SPV_switchGeometry3DName(v) v = v or this if v.RcType ~= rctype_Switch then return "Bad object type ["..RcType.."], '"..rctype_Switch.."' was expected" end local sideOfTrack = SwitchGeometry:upper() == "RIGHT" and "H" or "V" local suffix = SwitchNoseType:upper() == "FIXED" and "-FX" or "-BX" --Fixed or movable X-ing

LuaFunction.Name: _JBTKO_SPV_trackContinueCourse()
LuaFunction.Description: Returns a string holding either 'left' or 'right'. At present, 3-way switches (allowed in railML) are not modeled in RailCOMPLETE, i.e. ConnectionCourse being 'straight' leads to an error message.
LuaFunction.Formula: function _JBTKO_SPV_trackContinueCourse() if (ConnectionCourse == "right") then return "left" elseif (ConnectionCourse == "left") then return "right" elseif (ConnectionCourse == 'straight') then return "Cannot use 'straight' connection course in 2-way switch, use 'left' or 'right'",_warning else return "Bad connection course ["..ConnectionCourse.."]",_error end end
